ceiling_statement: Maximum determinism is: every trusted derivation is a total mathematical function of its committed input closure — byte-identical output on every re-execution, on any machine, at any time — where the closure explicitly includes every reified nondeterminism source (logical clock value, any seed, the parallel merge schedule, canonical orderings, and the pinned toolchain identity). Equivalently: the ONLY nondeterminism anywhere in the system lives outside the trusted path (LLM candidates, network fetches) and crosses into it solely as committed bytes. Byte-identity is the terminal point: no stronger equivalence than bit equality exists.
derivation: A computation's output can depend only on its inputs; therefore determinism is maximal exactly when the input set is closed — every read of wall-clock, RNG, scheduler order, hash-table iteration, address-dependent hashing, or filesystem enumeration is either banished from the trusted path or converted into a committed input. Nothing can exceed 'output = f(committed closure)': any residual dependence on an uncommitted quantity is, by definition, nondeterminism. Byte-identity across machines requires the implementation semantics be part of the closure (pinned SBCL version, IEEE-754 float behavior) — that is a closure item, not a weakening, so the ceiling stays model-independent. Two things NO feasible system can do, and the ceiling honestly excludes: determinizing the untrusted producers themselves (H1 confines them instead), and determinism against hardware faults (bit flips) — the attainable form there is detection by AX-13 recompute-and-compare, not prevention. This is also H5 stated as a maximum.
attainment_mechanism: (1) Clock: make the existing single time seat effective-deterministic-timestamp (systems/orchestrator-ai-core/config.lisp) mandatory by routing it through the CLOS :around constitutional barrier (systems/orchestrator-cli/constitutional-dispatch.lisp) so a wall-clock read in a trusted derivation cannot dispatch — structural elimination, not convention. (2) Ordering: canonical ordering seats already exist (systems/orchestrator-omega-modules/rdf-canonicalization.lisp; systems/orchestrator-model/article.lisp); extend to sorted directory enumeration and canonical hash-table traversal. (3) Parallelism: keep lparallel for speed but make the JOIN deterministic — the dependency graph's topological sort (systems/orchestrator-core/dependency-graph.lisp) fixes a committed merge order; workers complete in any real-time order, results are merged in the committed order, so the final state is schedule-independent (deterministic-join confluence). (4) Replay oracle: the exact-journal-prefix replay of source/legal-authority-receipt.lisp already demonstrates the exact-sequence-equality pattern; generalize it as the CI determinism gate: run twice, byte-compare. All SBCL-native, buildable today.
b0_gap: B0 already attains the ceiling locally (receipts replay exact journal-prefix with exact-seq equality; canonical ordering seats; dataset-stamp in capability-gate.lisp). Gaps per B0 map: omega activity timestamps default to wall-clock unless frozen (config.lisp seat exists but is opt-in, not structurally enforced); systems/orchestrator-core/parallel-executor.lisp has nondeterministic intra-tier order AND swallows per-stage errors to nil (verified at lines 71–81, 116–122) — an unordered, error-lossy join breaks replay; source/circuit-breaker.lisp decides on :system time, so a trusted control decision reads an uncommitted clock; kernel replay theorem T6 (authority-v2/kernel/admission-model.sexp) is specified but 0-proved.
lean_obligation: Theorem (deterministic step + confluent join): (1) the trusted small-step relation is a function: ∀ s a b, Step s a → Step s b → a = b, where the state includes the committed closure (logical clock, seeds, orderings) and NO other environment; (2) parallel schedule irrelevance: for the executor's tier semantics, any two interleavings σ₁ σ₂ admitted by the dependency DAG satisfy exec σ₁ s = exec σ₂ s (a diamond/commutation lemma over independent stages proved by Newman's lemma on the finite DAG); corollary: replay equality ∀ closure c, run c = run c reduces to reflexivity of a pure function `run : Closure → Output` — the Lean formalization defines run as a function, making nondeterminism unrepresentable.
